group.title: Nature and environment
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A sudden shaking of the ground caused by movement deep under the surface.
examples: The {earthquake} knocked down several old buildings.
wrong: The earthquake was so gentle that the sea stayed calm and nothing moved at all.

words.meaning: A mountain with a hole at the top that can throw out hot rock, gas and ash.
examples: Smoke was rising from the top of the {volcano}.
wrong: We cooled our drinks in the volcano because it was the coldest place on the island.

words.meaning: A thick forest in a hot place where it rains a lot.
examples: Many rare birds live in the {rainforest}.
wrong: The rainforest is dry all year, and it hardly ever rains there.

words.meaning: A high, steep wall of rock, often next to the sea.
examples: We stood at the edge of the {cliff} and looked down at the waves.
wrong: The cliff was so flat that children rode their bikes up it easily.

words.meaning: The top layer of the ground, where plants grow.
examples: Tomatoes grow well in rich, dark {soil}.
wrong: She poured the soil into a glass and drank it with lunch.

words.meaning: A plant such as wheat or rice that farmers grow in large amounts.
examples: Rice is the main {crop} in this region.
wrong: The farmer’s crop was the old truck he drove to town.

words.meaning: The foot of an animal such as a cat or dog, with claws and soft pads.
examples: The dog gave me its {paw} to shake.
wrong: The cat washed its face with the paw on the end of its tail.

words.meaning: An animal that feeds its babies on milk, such as a dog or a whale.
examples: The whale is the largest {mammal} on Earth.
wrong: A snake is a mammal because it lays eggs and has no hair.

words.meaning: A cold-blooded animal with dry skin covered in scales, such as a snake or lizard.
examples: A crocodile is a large {reptile}.
wrong: A parrot is a reptile because it has colorful feathers.

words.meaning: Any living animal, especially one that is strange or unknown.
examples: Strange {creatures} live at the bottom of the sea.
wrong: The table is a creature that eats and breathes.

words.meaning: A home that a bird builds from sticks and grass for its eggs.
examples: The bird laid three eggs in its {nest}.
wrong: Birds build their nests at the bottom of the river, under the water.

words.meaning: To chase and catch wild animals to kill or eat them.
examples: Lions usually {hunt} at night.
wrong: The wolves hunted by lying asleep all day and never looking for food.

words.meaning: Paper, bottles and other rubbish left on the ground in a public place.
examples: Please put your {litter} in the bin.
wrong: The park was full of litter, so it looked perfectly clean.

words.meaning: The slow rise in the temperature of the Earth’s air and seas.
examples: {Global warming} is making the ice at the poles melt.
wrong: Because of global warming, the Earth is getting much colder every year.

words.meaning: A line of colorful rock-like material built by tiny sea animals in warm, shallow water.
examples: We swam with bright fish over the {coral reef}.
wrong: The coral reef grows high on the snowy mountain tops.

words.meaning: To produce open flowers.
examples: The roses {bloom} in early summer.
wrong: The tree bloomed, so all its branches were bare with no flowers.

words.meaning: Able to grow plenty of healthy plants.
examples: The valley has {fertile} land, so farmers grow lots of food there.
wrong: The fertile field was so poor that nothing would grow in it.

words.meaning: The land along the edge of a sea or lake.
examples: We walked along the {shore} and collected shells.
wrong: The shore is the deepest part of the ocean, far from any land.

words.meaning: The regular rise and fall of the sea level each day.
examples: At low {tide} you can walk out to the island.
wrong: The tide is the wind that blows through the forest.

words.meaning: A huge mass of ice that moves very slowly down a mountain.
examples: The {glacier} has shrunk a lot in fifty years.
wrong: The glacier melted in the hot desert sand where it formed.

words.meaning: A wild area of land where nobody lives or farms.
examples: They spent a week hiking in the {wilderness}.
wrong: The wilderness was full of shops, offices and busy roads.

words.meaning: An animal that kills and eats other animals.
examples: The shark is a dangerous {predator}.
wrong: The rabbit is a predator that hunts lions for food.

words.meaning: An animal that is hunted and eaten by another animal.
examples: Mice are common {prey} for owls.
wrong: The eagle was the mouse’s prey, so the mouse ate it.

words.meaning: A group of birds or sheep together.
examples: A {flock} of geese flew over the lake.
wrong: A flock is one single sheep standing alone in a field.

words.meaning: A large group of animals such as cows or elephants that live together.
examples: A {herd} of cows was crossing the road.
wrong: The herd was just one lonely elephant.

words.meaning: From or in the hot, wet parts of the world near the middle of the Earth.
examples: Bananas and mangoes are {tropical} fruits.
wrong: Polar bears love the tropical cold of the North Pole.

words.meaning: A very strong storm with violent winds, especially over the sea.
examples: The {hurricane} destroyed hundreds of homes along the coast.
wrong: The hurricane was so calm that the leaves didn’t move.

words.meaning: A large mass of earth and rocks that falls down a hill.
examples: Heavy rain caused a {landslide} that blocked the road.
wrong: The landslide carried the rocks slowly up to the top of the hill.

words.meaning: One of the very large areas of land on Earth, such as Africa or Asia.
examples: Australia is both a country and a {continent}.
wrong: My street is the biggest continent in the world.

words.meaning: A large fire that spreads quickly and out of control through forests or grass.
examples: The {wildfire} burned for days before it was put out.
wrong: The wildfire was a small candle burning safely on the table.

words.meaning: To make air, water or land dirty and harmful.
examples: Factories {pollute} the river with chemicals.
wrong: The new cars polluted the city by making the air cleaner.

words.meaning: The process of treating used things such as paper and glass so they can be used again.
examples: We put bottles and cans in the {recycling} bin.
wrong: Recycling means burying old bottles so they can never be used again.

words.meaning: An area of soft, wet land partly covered with water and plants.
examples: Alligators live in the {swamp}.
wrong: The swamp was the driest place in the whole desert.

words.meaning: Useful things found in nature, such as water, wood, oil and minerals.
examples: The country is rich in {natural resources} like oil and gold.
wrong: Plastic chairs and video games are natural resources found in forests.

words.meaning: To become less and less common until none are left.
examples: Many kinds of animals {died out} after the ice age.
wrong: The birds died out, so now there are more of them than ever.

words.meaning: A large area of land protected by the government for its nature and wildlife.
examples: We saw bears and wolves in the {national park}.
wrong: They built a huge shopping mall in the middle of the national park to protect it.

words.meaning: To travel to a different place at a certain time of year, as birds do.
examples: Many birds {migrate} south for the winter.
wrong: The birds migrated by staying in the same tree all year.

words.meaning: To sleep through the winter, as some animals do.
examples: Bears {hibernate} in caves during the cold months.
wrong: The bear hibernated by running around all winter looking for food.

words.meaning: The hard, pointed mouth of a bird.
examples: The bird cracked the seed with its {beak}.
wrong: The dog wagged its beak when it saw me.

words.meaning: The thick, soft hair that covers some animals.
examples: The cat has soft white {fur}.
wrong: Fish keep warm in the water with their thick fur.
